correctness.rationale: For each fixed original-edge matching, toggling the least uncovered pendant edge gives an acyclic Boolean-fiber Morse matching; the only unpaired faces are the perfect original matchings. The ordinary reduction has one critical zero-cell and one critical (m-1)-cell per perfect matching, which are maximal. Integral cycles built as joins of reduced two-term zero-cycles have a Kronecker pairing with maximal base-edge face cocycles, making them primitive. Endpoint substitutions are boundaries; factor permutations produce determinant signs. Independent finite checks cover 190 Morse matchings, 162 mod-two homologies and 54 Lefschetz traces. All quantifiers, n>=1 and m=1, checked.

value.rationale: For arbitrary finite simple base graphs (not only outerplanar), the theorem turns a natural exact graph invariant—the count of perfect matchings—into an integral topological sphere count and supplies canonical primitive cycles and full automorphism signs. The module distinguishes graph symmetries that ordinary Betti numbers cannot; the formula applies to nonplanar and heterogeneous/disconnected cases and supports further equivariant calculations. The result is not a textbook exercise, merely a computation, or an arbitrary finite slice.
